_about: Three critical frames on cultural institutions, shown on the records they apply to as critiques of kind 'theory'. Each frame holds a list of short verbatim 'quotes', each with its author, source and url, all shown on the page; the works it rests on are listed under 'rests_on' for the editor. (A frame may instead hold a paraphrase 'summary', shown with no author or citation; none does now.) tools/attach_critiques.py writes them; re-running replaces them. A quote may carry 'parts' instead of one 'text': several verbatim passages from the same source, each shown as its own paragraph, optionally after a short 'lead' of reported context (never in quotation marks).

frames.target: Museums of modern and contemporary art, biennials and festivals

quotes.text: Thus, our art museums became huge garbage cans of history in which things were kept and exhibited that had no use anymore in real life: sacral images of past religions or status objects of past lifestyles.
quotes.author: Boris Groys
quotes.source: ‘Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk’, e-flux journal 50, December 2013

quotes.text: A new curator is a new dictator who erases the traces of the previous dictatorship. In this way, contemporary museums continually morph from spaces for permanent collections into stages for temporary curatorial projects—temporary Gesamtkunstwerks.
quotes.author: Boris Groys
quotes.source: ‘Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk’, e-flux journal 50, December 2013

frames.impact: Read a museum's event calendar and curatorial turnover against what it actually keeps, conserves and pays for.
rests_on: Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk, e-flux journal 50 (2013)

frames.strategy: The gift that follows the taking
frames.target: Institutions funded by donors whose money carries a flag

quotes.text: Remember Andrew Carnegie, who employed a private army to suppress organised labour in his steelworks and then distributed large parts of his wealth for educational, cultural and humanitarian causes, proving that, although a man of steel, he had a heart of gold? In the same way, today’s liberal communists give away with one hand what they grabbed with the other.
quotes.author: Slavoj Žižek
quotes.source: ‘Nobody has to be vile’, London Review of Books 28/7, 6 April 2006

quotes.text: According to liberal communist ethics, the ruthless pursuit of profit is counteracted by charity: charity is part of the game, a humanitarian mask hiding the underlying economic exploitation.
quotes.author: Slavoj Žižek
quotes.source: ‘Nobody has to be vile’, London Review of Books 28/7, 6 April 2006

frames.impact: Where a flag names an industry, ask what the gift was repairing, and for whom.
rests_on: Nobody has to be vile, London Review of Books 28/7 (2006)
First as Tragedy, Then as Farce (2009), the RSA lecture of the same year

frames.target: Biennials, festivals and touring exhibitions, and the cities that host them

parts.lead: Closing the sixth Moscow Biennale, he began by asking the hall to look at the money in their pockets:
parts.text: Take a euro note out and have a look at it. […] Just look at it aesthetically. What do you see? A very boring design.

parts.lead: The bridges and arches on the notes are ‘figments of some second-rate artist’s imagination’, he said, because the EU’s members could not agree on whose cultural treasures should appear on them. Worse than art created by committee, though, are the attempts of bureaucrats and big businesses to appropriate it:
parts.text: Art must not be anodyne, culture cannot be decorative. [Artists] should be feared by the powerful in our society; if you are not, you are not doing your job properly.

parts.lead: In an aside, he also knocked
parts.text: forums in which the stars are the postmodernist curators inviting economists to give a lecture to artists.

quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.source: keynote closing the 6th Moscow Biennale, 1 October 2015, as reported by The Art Newspaper, 3 October 2015

quotes.text: Documenta took a great deal more from Athens—from both its private and public sector—than it gave. […] When Documenta comes here and talks about neoliberalism with no mention of Deutsche Bank, Société Générale, the awful Troika process, the Eurogroup, etc., it is choosing to be irrelevant.
quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.source: ‘We Come Bearing Gifts’, in conversation with iLiana Fokianaki on documenta 14 Athens, art-agenda / e-flux criticism, 7 June 2017

frames.impact: Read a festival's balance with its host city, and its critique against its sponsor list.
